newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - ACT Brumbies determined to crush Otago.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - ACT Brumbies determined to crush Otago.

text.p: AUCKLAND, April 16 - The ACT Brumbies left Auckland for Invercargill on Wednesday thoroughly determined to lift their performance levels against the Otago Highlanders in their Super 12 match on Friday night, NZPA reports.
ACT were beaten 41-29 by the Auckland Blues last weekend and coach Rod Macqueen said his team had spent the last few days pondering their poor performance at Pukekohe.
"Hindsight is an easy thing, it could be a number of reasons but we don't know why we didn't play well," Macqueen said today.
"Auckland played well, we don't doubt that, but at the same time we didn't play to our standards.
"Whether we were tentative, lethargic or whatever, we're aware we need to show more urgency and passion in our next game and get back to playing the way we know we can."

The Brumbies, who have stayed in Auckland until today, trained well this week with the only casualty being utility back Rod Kafer who fractured a cheekbone at training on Monday. He has been replaced in the reserves by Liam O'Connor, who joined the squad yesterday.
ACT's biggest interest in the Otago team was All Black openside flanker Josh Kronfeld's return.
However Kronfeld, who was recovering from a corked thigh which he aggravated in a club match last weekend, is a week away from returning to the Highlanders.
"Josh is training with the team at the moment but he's still a bit sore and we didn't want to risk him," Highlanders manager Des Smith said.
"We'd be looking to have him back in a week or so, but at the moment we want him to recover completely."

Otago: Matthew Carrington, Jeff Wilson, Romi Ropati, Manasa Bari, To'o Vaega, Tony Brown, Stu Forster, Taine Randell (captain), Kupu Vanisi, John Blaikie, Steve Gordon, Isotola Maka, Nick Moore, Anton Oliver, Carl Hoeft.
